about: Rapier's Water palette: eighteen watercolours chosen from what working painters carry and love: a warm and a cool of each primary, a true warm red, a deep cool red and a magenta, a violet, the blues from sky to turquoise, the greens from emerald to forest, the earths, a grey, a true black and a white. Each is a single pigment named by Colour Index (Sap Green is the one named mixture, because that is how it is sold) and carries the properties paint makers and colour writers publish: how it looks at full strength (masstone) and in a thin wash, how opaque it is, how much it granulates and stains, and the wavelengths where it absorbs. tools/generate-water-color.py fits the absorbance spectrum to the two appearances through Rapier's own display model and writes draw/water-pigments.mjs. The numbers are Rapier's own, tuned against published swatch appearances; they are not measurements of any maker's paint.

pigments.name: Hansa Yellow Light
pigments.note: The cool lemon yellow: bright and transparent; with a blue that leans green it makes the cleanest greens.

pigments.name: New Gamboge
pigments.note: The warm golden yellow, as one pigment (PY153): transparent and a little orange where the lemon is cool; clean oranges with a red, warm greens with a blue.

pigments.name: Pyrrol Scarlet
pigments.note: The true warm red: bright, transparent and a little orange, where cadmium red goes dull.

pigments.name: Permanent Alizarin Crimson
pigments.note: The deep cool red: a dark, transparent crimson for shadows and, with a green, rich neutrals.

pigments.name: Quinacridone Magenta
pigments.note: The cool pink-purple red: transparent and staining; with ultramarine it makes the brightest violets.

pigments.name: Dioxazine Violet
pigments.note: The violet: very strong and transparent; a touch tints a whole wash.

pigments.name: French Ultramarine
pigments.note: The warm blue: transparent and granulating; greys with burnt sienna, soft violets with a rose.

pigments.name: Cerulean Blue
pigments.note: The sky blue: soft, granulating and a little opaque, with a chalky body.

pigments.name: Phthalo Turquoise
pigments.note: The turquoise: a very strong, staining blue-green for water and cool greens; a touch goes a long way.

pigments.name: Phthalo Green
pigments.note: The cool emerald green: very strong and staining; with a yellow it makes every foliage green a landscape needs.

pigments.name: Sap Green
pigments.note: The leaf green painters buy by name: a natural, warm, yellowish foliage green straight from the tube (a mixture of a phthalo green and a yellow).

pigments.name: Perylene Green
pigments.note: The deep forest green: a dark, transparent green, nearly black at full strength, for the shadows in foliage; with a red it makes rich darks.

pigments.name: Yellow Ochre
pigments.note: The yellow earth: soft, semi-opaque and a little granular.

pigments.name: Burnt Sienna
pigments.note: The warm red-brown earth: transparent and granulating; the partner of blue for greys.

pigments.name: Burnt Umber
pigments.note: The dark warm brown: falls away smoothly into the red, and deepens any mix.

pigments.name: Davy's Gray
pigments.note: The tube grey: powdered slate, a soft semi-opaque neutral grey with a faint olive cast that granulates a little; it greys a mix without the weight of black.

pigments.name: Lamp Black
pigments.note: The true black: black at the default dose and in a wash a dark neutral grey.

pigments.name: White Gouache
pigments.note: Opaque white for lights, highlights and lifting back.
